build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: Primary mechanic A is complete and playable: Ability gate and progression system. Score 0 if it is absent, decorative, or cannot be exercised through player input. Score 1 requires connected state changes and visible success/failure consequences in a playable flow.

Primary mechanic B is complete and connected to A: Auto-mapping and room tracking. Score 0 if it is absent, decorative, or cannot be exercised through player input. Score 1 requires connected state changes and visible success/failure consequences in a playable flow.

Primary mechanics C and D both affect live play: 2D platformer controller with ability expansion; Interconnected zone and fast travel system. Score 0 if it is absent, decorative, or cannot be exercised through player input. Score 1 requires connected state changes and visible success/failure consequences in a playable flow.

At least four supporting systems are implemented and connected: Ability gate system: passages tagged with required ability; Movement ability tree: double jump, dash, wall climb, grapple, etc.; Auto-mapping with room completion tracking; Boss room with ability drop on defeat; Collectible tracking per room (hidden items, upgrades); Save point system with fast travel unlock; NPC hint system for ability-locked paths; Upgrade currency from enemy drops. Score 0 if the content is missing or differs only through labels or color swaps. Score 1 requires functionally distinct content that changes player decisions.

Build at least three connected locations with distinct discoveries, one optional route, an escalating objective chain, and a final resolution changed by player actions. Score 0 if the content is missing or differs only through labels or color swaps. Score 1 requires functionally distinct content that changes player decisions.

The rules layer maintains resources, objectives, selection, danger, progress, and outcome without relying on DOM text as the source of truth. Score 0 if the content is missing or differs only through labels or color swaps. Score 1 requires functionally distinct content that changes player decisions.

A three-stage progression teaches the core mechanic, combines systems under greater pressure, and ends with a mastery scenario plus a working replay flow. Score 0 if the content is missing or differs only through labels or color swaps. Score 1 requires functionally distinct content that changes player decisions.

The HUD clearly communicates current objective, critical resources, selected target or mode, progress, and danger in stable regions. Score 0 if essential information or feedback is missing, unreadable, overlapping, or disconnected from live game state at 1280x720.

Important actions have immediate, distinguishable feedback for valid input, invalid input, success, damage or failure, and state changes. Score 0 if essential information or feedback is missing, unreadable, overlapping, or disconnected from live game state at 1280x720.

The full loop is connected: styled start flow, playable systems, escalation, final success/failure state, and retry navigation work without page reload. Score 0 if essential information or feedback is missing, unreadable, overlapping, or disconnected from live game state at 1280x720.

The project has a coherent authored art direction: Authored landmarks, layered routes, environmental storytelling, clear interaction highlights, and lighting that guides exploration without flattening the scene. Score 0 if the presentation is dominated by default controls, unlit primitives, inconsistent materials, or abrupt unanimated state changes.

The 2D side-scrolling composition uses deliberate lighting, contrast, depth or layering, and themed landmarks instead of an empty default scene. Score 0 if the presentation is dominated by default controls, unlit primitives, inconsistent materials, or abrupt unanimated state changes.

Interactive actors, targets, hazards, tools, and UI symbols have readable silhouettes and visibly different functional states. Score 0 if the presentation is dominated by default controls, unlit primitives, inconsistent materials, or abrupt unanimated state changes.

Movement, impacts, transitions, alerts, completion moments, and interface changes use smooth multi-frame animation, particles, camera treatment, or synchronized audio feedback. Score 0 if the presentation is dominated by default controls, unlit primitives, inconsistent materials, or abrupt unanimated state changes.
